figures.caption: Diverted 550-cell fresh-read solution after three accepted Newton steps: fresh residual 1.00e-11, converged true. Bank flux is solid blue above the dashed grey analytic oracle on the same psi levels, -0.060194, -0.045963, -0.031731, -0.017500, -0.003269, 0.010962 and 0.025193 Wb. The black outline is the wall, which bounds the cropped canvas. The bank axis is a filled blue triangle and its admitted saddle a filled blue cross; the direct analytic Newton references are an outlined grey triangle and diamond. The wider outlines keep nearly coincident null sets separately legible.

rubric.contrast: pass: the only text is the two-column figure legend, rendered pure black on pure white. The bank blue #3366CC measures about 5.4:1 and the oracle grey #676767 about 5.7:1 against white, both above 4.5:1 at 14 pt, and the two series are separated by dash pattern as well as by hue, so neither depends on lightness alone to be told from the other.
rubric.data_ink: pass: the picture is two contour families, one wall outline and four null marks. There is no tick, tick label, spine, gridline, title or annotation; the poloidal axes are off, so the contours, the wall and the margin crop carry all the meaning.
rubric.decoration: pass: nothing on the canvas is decorative. No gradient, no background fill, no confidence band, no shadow, no themed styling, and no fill between contours; the white field is empty and the only inked objects are data or the wall.
rubric.label_collision: pass: the legend is the only text and it sits wholly inside the top band of the canvas, with two clean columns, a gap between the columns and no row touching another; the panel's data begins well below it. Nothing is clipped at any edge, no label overlaps another, and no text is placed over a contour, the wall or a null mark.
rubric.legibility: pass at the delivered render (attached image-0.png, 1400x2039 native): the seven shared psi levels read as one nested family of closed loops inside the wall, the blue bank stroke is continuous along its whole length, and the two series are separable everywhere they separate. Both null pairs are identifiable: at the centre a filled blue triangle sits inside an outlined grey triangle, and near the bottom a filled blue cross sits inside an outlined grey diamond, so the nearly coincident reference and solved stationary points stay distinct. Remaining readability costs are recorded as non-blocking findings rather than folded into this verdict: the reference reads as a fringe where the fields agree, the panel leaves blank bands either side, and no curve carries its level.
rubric.table_form: pass: the content is spatial - two flux fields, their stationary points and a first-wall boundary in the poloidal plane - where relative position is the information. Nothing here is a list of numbers a table would serve better; the seven psi levels the caption lists stay in the caption where they belong.

findings.summary: The analytic oracle is drawn beneath the bank field at 4.5 pt (zorder 3) while the solved field is drawn over it at 3.0 pt (zorder 4), so wherever the two agree - which is most of the panel, since agreement is what the record exists to show - the reference survives only as a thin grey fringe protruding along either side of the blue stroke, and its own curve cannot be followed there. The oracle is traceable as a separate trace only where the fields visibly diverge, along the outer right and the bottom. The legend keys 'oracle flux' as a full-thickness dashed swatch, which is not the fringe a reader meets on the panel, so the legend has to be inferred rather than matched. The agreement itself is legible, which is why this does not block; drawing the reference at or below the subject's weight, or relying on the dash pattern for separation instead of on a wider stroke, would let a reader follow both curves.

The canvas is a portrait 7.2x10.5 in with the legend pinned in the top band (top=0.79) and the poloidal axes set to equal aspect, so the drawn plasma spans roughly x 250-1150 of the 1400 px width - about 64 per cent - leaving a blank band of about 18 per cent on each side, and the legend occupies the top fifth of the height. At the page width the figure renders at, the two null outlines the caption spends a sentence distinguishing (a 7 pt blue triangle inside a 14 pt grey outline; a filled blue cross inside a grey diamond) fall to a few pixels each. The figure reads correctly at its intrinsic size, so this does not block; cropping the horizontal margins to the wall would let the panel use more of the page.

The seven levels are computed from the analytic field and listed only in the caption, and because the poloidal axes and all labels are off, no contour on the panel is identified by level. A reader who wants to know which curve is -0.060194 Wb and which is 0.025193 Wb has to count contours from the axis outward, and the caption's claim that both fields sit on the same levels rests on the visual coincidence of the strokes alone. The coincidence is in fact visible, so this does not block; one direct label per contour, or a stated level ordering in the caption, would make the shared-level claim checkable from the picture.
